The **melody** is the tune: the line you would sing back. These are the words for describing one.

## 1. Direction and movement

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Rising / ascending** | going up |
| **Falling / descending** | going down |
| **Conjunct** | moving by step, to the next note up or down |
| **Disjunct** | moving by leap, jumping over notes |
| **Range** | the distance from the lowest note to the highest: *narrow* or *wide* |

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Conjunct, narrow range
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
C D E F|E D E C|D E D C|C4|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Disjunct, wide range
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
C c G, e|A, a E c'|G, g C,2|C4|]
</script></div>
:::

## 2. Repetition and its relatives

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Repetition** | the same idea again, unchanged |
| **Sequence** | the same idea again, starting on a higher or lower note |
| **Imitation** | one part copies an idea another part has just played, often at a different pitch |
| **Ostinato** | a short idea repeated over and over (in the bass it is a *ground bass* or a *riff*) |
| **Contrast** | something completely different |

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Sequence: the same shape, a step higher each time
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
CDEC D2 z2|DEFD E2 z2|EFGE F2 z2|G8|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Imitation: the lower part copies the upper
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
V:1
GABG c2 G2|ABcA d2 A2|G8|
V:2 clef=bass
z8|G,A,B,G, C2 G,2|A,B,CA, D4|
</script></div>
:::

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="104" data-style="rock"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Ostinato: one measure, four times, while the chords change
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:Am
"Am"A,2 CE A2 GE|"F"A,2 CE A2 GE|"C"A,2 CE A2 GE|"G"A,2 CE A2 GE|]
</script></div>

## 3. What the melody is made of

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Scalic** | runs up and down the scale |
| **Triadic** | uses the notes of the chords (broken chords) |
| **Chromatic** | uses notes outside the key, often moving by [half step]{.nn} |
| **Pentatonic** | uses only five notes |
| **Ornamented** | decorated with trills, mordents, turns, grace notes |

::: {.ax-pair}
<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Triadic
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"C"C E G c|"G"B G D G|"C"c G E C|]
</script></div>

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="90"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Chromatic
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
E ^D E ^F G ^G A ^A|B c ^c d ^d e2 z|]
</script></div>
:::

Ornaments, with how each period played them: [Grace Notes and Ornaments](grace-notes-ornaments.qmd),
[Ornaments by Period](ornaments-by-period.qmd).

## 4. Intervals

An **interval** is the distance between two notes. Count the letter names, **including both the first and the last**:
C up to E is C-D-E, three letters, a 3rd.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="80"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:From C: 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, octave
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
C D C E|C F C G|C A C B|C c3|]
</script></div>

## 5. Scale degrees

Every note of the scale has a number and a name:

| 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tonic | supertonic | mediant | subdominant | dominant | submediant | leading note (leading tone) |

The tonic is home; the leading note pulls up to it; the dominant is the strongest note after the tonic. The same numbers
in Roman numerals name the chords built on them (see [Harmony](elements-harmony.qmd#chords)).

## 6. Writing your own

The [Melody](compose-melody.qmd) and [Motif](compose-motif.qmd) lessons build a tune from these tools: a shape with one
high point, mostly steps with a few leaps, a motif repeated and sequenced, and an ending on the tonic.
